end.summary:
Practised naming common non-metals and identifying their states.
Connected non-metals with uses in pencils, water treatment, iodised salt, fertilisers, rocket fuel, balloons and chip packets.
Answered that oxygen is about 21% of air and explained nitrogen in fertilisers and chip packets.
Explored oxygen, carbon and nitrogen as essential to living things; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Pari practised classifying non-metals by state and linking them to everyday uses. They explained the roles of oxygen in breathing, carbon dioxide in photosynthesis, and nitrogen in plant proteins and fertilisers; one mix-up about carbon was corrected later by distinguishing carbon from carbon dioxide (correctAfterLastSeen). At home, ask Pari to make a three-column chart for oxygen, carbon and nitrogen: source, role in living things, and one everyday use.
